**Summary:** Refactor `tests/test_triage_audit.py` to target the new descriptor-driven handler API. Add new test files for `AuditResult` dataclass/parser and handler unit tests. Maintain coverage for cooldown (caller concern), blocked items, Discord integration, and auto-completion.

- [ ] Existing 13 test scenarios from `tests/test_triage_audit.py` are preserved or intentionally replaced with equivalent coverage targeting the new handler API

- [ ] New tests for extended auto-completion checks (PR merge, CI status, PR comments, children, deps)
- [ ] All external calls mocked (`wl`, `opencode run`, `gh pr view`, `gh api`)
- [ ] Test coverage for audit-related code paths >= prior level as measured by `pytest --cov`

- New `tests/test_audit_result.py` for AuditResult dataclass and parser

- SA-0MM8W553C1WK7JE5 (audit_result handler)
- SA-0MM8W5EXT1BXC7PB (audit_fail handler)
- SA-0MM8W5U8C0QGGXTD (close_with_audit handler)

- Refactored test files

# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally
  closes work items only after the `dev`→`main` release.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MN1M2B810I9YC0U** – Validate Playwright Distrobox compatibility spike (completed)
- **SA-0MPON9P8Z0062VBL** – Child work items created by /plan should start at intake_complete stage (completed)
- **SA-0MKXYO42T0FC6IJR** – Isolated work environments for parallel work (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: container, directory, make, project, right (+3 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)

## Goal

Execute the 24-hour experiment: apply the STE100 instruction to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, let it run for 24h, measure metrics, produce comparison report, and revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add the sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md (verified via grep).
2. Record exact wall-clock T0 and commit hash.
3. Run analysis at T0+24h for both [T0-24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) windows.
4. Produce comparison report at `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` with:
   - Metrics table (session count, duration, tokens, cost for both windows)
   - Delta percentages and direction for each metric
   - Notable outliers (output-token-limit errors, extreme sessions)
   - Project and model breakdown
   - One-line interpretation per metric
5. Revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (verified via grep).
6. Record revert commit hash.

## Steps

1. Start parent implementation
2. Implement child tasks first (analysis script + tests)
3. Add STE100 sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev, record T0
4. Wait 24 hours (or set reminder/automation)
5. Run analysis for baseline window [T0-24h, T0)
6. Run analysis for experiment window [T0, T0+24h)
7. Generate comparison report
8. Revert AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev
9. Record results on work item
10. Clean up worktree

## Related

Dependent on: SA-0MU9VSL250092LTY (Build analysis script), SA-0MU9VT5HI001LHKY (Add tests).

# Intake brief — implement.py live-repo guard ownership parity

**Headline:** `implement.py`'s test runs must adopt the canonical live-repo guard ownership used by `run_tests.py` (outer snapshot guard + `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` marker), so no nested or cascaded run is left unguarded now the original teardown crash is fixed.

> The work-item title describes the originally reported symptom (a crash). That
> crash is now fixed and shipped (SA-0MUH5KFDV002ORSS). This brief re-scopes the
> residual work to the guard-ownership divergence the symptom exposed.

## Problem statement

`implement.py`'s test execution (`run_tests`) invokes the suite through
`test_cache.run_cached` with a direct `pytest`/suite command and **never sets
`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`**, and it runs **no outer snapshot guard** of its own.
`run_tests.py`, by contrast, sets the marker *and* owns the checkout via an
outer pre/post snapshot. The two paths therefore disagree about who guards the
checkout: direct `pytest` (via the repo-root `conftest.py`) arms the inner
`skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` plugin, while `run_tests.py` stands that inner
guard down and guards itself.

The originally reported crash (the inner guard's `pytest_runtest_teardown`
running before the `monkeypatch` fixture was undone) is **already fixed** by
SA-0MUH5KFDV002ORSS (`trylast=True`), so AC1 as originally written already
passes. The remaining defect is the ownership divergence: when
`implement.py`'s test runs are started with the marker already set in the
environment (e.g. a nested/cascaded run under `run_tests.py` or an audit
subprocess), the inner guard stands down *and* `implement.py` arms no outer
guard — leaving the checkout **unguarded**. That is precisely the class of gap
the original issue warned about.

## Users

- **AI implement agents** — run `implement.py finish`, whose full-suite gate must
  be reliably guarded without an externally exported `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`.
- **Producers / reviewers** — rely on a green finish gate meaning "the suite
  passed in a checkout that did not mutate", regardless of which entry point ran
  it.

Example user stories:
- As an implement agent, I want `implement.py`'s test runs to use the same
  live-repo guard ownership as `run_tests.py`, so a green gate always implies the
  checkout was verified for mutation.
- As a producer, I want a single guard implementation so a fix in one path cannot
  leave the other silently unguarded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (re-scoped to parity)** `implement.py`'s test execution runs under the
  canonical live-repo guard ownership contract: an authoritative guard owns the
  checkout on every run, and the `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` marker is set/consumed
  consistently so no run leaves both the outer and inner guard disarmed.
  *Verification:* a test that starts implement's test execution with
  `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` already set shows mutation detection still armed (or
  that the run is delegated to the guard-owning canonical runner).
- **AC2 (regression test)** A regression test asserts the ownership contract at
  the boundary between `implement.py` and the canonical runner — i.e. that the
  marker is set for the inner pytest invocation *and* an outer guard is armed,
  **or** that `implement.py` delegates to the canonical `run_tests.py` runner
  (which owns both). *Verification:* new test in `skill/implement/tests/` and/or
  `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`.
- **AC3 (no double-guard / real detection)** No double-guard reporting: a clean
  run reports no guard failure; a deliberate mid-run mutation (tracked file
  change or ref move) is detected and yields a non-zero result through the
  owning guard. *Verification:* a mutation test plus a clean-run assertion.
- **AC4 (behaviour preserved)** Existing `implement.py` test behaviour is
  unchanged: changed-scope selection, named groups, `run_cached` caching keys and
  `scope` metadata, host-wide test-semaphore pacing, the `skipped`/`tooling`
  result contract, and graceful degradation on partial skill installs.
  *Verification:* existing `tests/test_implement_run_tests_*.py` suites stay
  green.
- **AC5 (docs)** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (notably the guard-ownership description in `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, and the implement skill docs).
- **AC6 (full suite)** The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

> **AC1 wording (producer decision Q3=a):** re-scoped from "finish gate passes
> without an externally-set marker" (already satisfied by SA-0MUH5KFDV002ORSS)
> to guard-ownership parity.

## Constraints

- **Do not set the marker without an outer guard.** The issue's literal proposal
  (just set `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE=1` in `implement.py`) would stand the *only*
  armed guard down and violate AC3. The producer chose the canonical-runner route
  (Q2=A) precisely to avoid this.
- **Single guard implementation.** Prefer delegating to the canonical
  `run_tests.py` guard over duplicating snapshot logic in `implement.py`.
- **Preserve caching and pacing.** Any delegation must keep cache sharing with
  `run_tests.py` (identical keys / `scope` metadata) and the host-wide "test"
  semaphore.
- **Graceful degradation.** `implement.py` treats the test skill as optional
  (partial installs). The parity mechanism must not make `implement.py` depend
  hard on the test skill being present.
- **No test-weakening.** No skips/xfails/retries to reach green.

## Existing state

- Crash fixed and shipped: SA-0MUH5KFDV002ORSS added
  `@pytest.hookimpl(trylast=True)` to the guard's `pytest_runtest_teardown`.
  Verified at HEAD: `pytest skill/audit/tests/test_audit_queue_integration.py`
  with `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` unset → `6 passed`, clean finish.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `run_tests`, `_run_resolved_suite`,
  `_run_commands`, `_run_changed_scope_pytest` all execute via `run_cmd` /
  `run_cached` with inherited `os.environ`; no marker set; no `snapshot` /
  `live_repo` reference anywhere in the file.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — the canonical runner: owns the outer
  snapshot guard (`snapshot_repo_state` / `_detect_live_repo_mutation`) and
  sets/pops `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` around `run_all`.
- `conftest.py` (repo root) — loads `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` by file
  location and arms it for direct `pytest` invocations.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — the inner plugin; `MARKER_ENV =
  LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`; no-op when the marker is set.

## Desired change

Bring `implement.py`'s test execution under the canonical guard-ownership
contract (**producer decision Q2=A**): route it through the canonical
`run_tests.py` runner so that runner's outer snapshot guard owns the checkout and
sets `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`, standing the inner conftest guard down. Where a
full subprocess delegation is impractical, the equivalent is to factor the guard
ownership into a shared helper consumed by both `implement.py` and `run_tests.py`
so there is exactly one implementation and no path is left unguarded — but the
outcome must satisfy AC1–AC3, not merely move the marker.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Route `run_tests` / `_run_resolved_suite` / `_run_commands` / `_run_changed_scope_pytest` through the canonical runner or a shared guard-ownership helper; preserve cache/pacing/result contracts.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Canonical runner + outer guard; may need a reusable entry point (programmatic API) so `implement.py` can delegate without shelling out; keep marker semantics.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — Inner plugin; document/confirm the marker contract; may host the shared guard-ownership helper if not placed in the test skill.
- `conftest.py` — Repo-root arming of the inner guard; behaviour must remain correct for direct `pytest`.
- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` — Add the ownership-parity regression/mutation tests.
- `skill/implement/tests/` (new test module, e.g. `test_implement_guard_ownership.py`) — Assert `implement.py` arms the guard / delegates to the canonical runner.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` / relevant docs — Document the single guard-ownership contract.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: full delegation changes `implement.py`'s result/caching contract.** Mitigation: AC4 pins changed-scope, cache keys/`scope` metadata, pacing, and the `skipped`/`tooling` contract; delegate via a programmatic entry point rather than scraping CLI stdout where possible.
- **Risk: partial skill installs.** `implement.py` treats the test skill as optional and degrades to legacy convention detection. Mitigation: keep the delegation optional; fall back to the current (inner-guard) behaviour with a warning when the test skill is unavailable.
- **Risk: duplicated guard logic re-appears.** If a shared helper is used instead of subprocess delegation, ensure it is a single implementation consumed by both paths — not a second copy.
- **Risk: scope creep.** The two open guard-flakiness items (SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU, SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH) are adjacent but out of scope; they remain tracked separately and must not be pulled into this item.
- **Assumption:** the marker/`trylast` fix (SA-0MUH5KFDV002ORSS) stays in place; this item does not touch teardown ordering.
- **Assumption:** "canonical runner" permits either delegating to `run_tests.py`'s guard-owning path or extracting a shared ownership helper, provided AC1–AC3 hold.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUH5KFDV002ORSS** — Fix live-repo guard teardown ordering (fixed the
  teardown/monkeypatch crash; makes AC1-as-written pass). *Predecessor.*
- **SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ** — Repo-root conftest live-repo guard (the inner net).
- **SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H** — `run_tests.py` live-repo snapshot guard (the outer net).
- **SA-0MUG47DYG006TV40** — child-audit cascade recursion marker propagation.
- **SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU** — test-suite flakiness under concurrent load (guard
  false positives).
- **SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH** — guard shared-refs/stash false positives across
  worktrees.
- Discovered during **SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1**.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope).** Given the crash is already fixed, should this item (a) stay
  open to fix guard-ownership parity, (b) be closed as superseded, or (c) be

## Summary

The 2026-09-26 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident (SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX) was rooted in a repository-override git environment variable exported into agent/test sessions by a launcher **outside** the `skill/` tree. Defence-in-depth now neutralises the *effect* at every in-repo execution path, but the launcher can still export a live-repo `GIT_DIR` (plus `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`) into the **pre-scrub** environment of any process that calls `git` directly. This item investigates that export and removes or scopes it at its source.

## Problem statement

On 2026-09-26 an orphaned audit fan-out inherited `GIT_DIR=<live worktree git dir>`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` and `GIT_PREFIX=` from a launcher outside the `skill/` tree. The in-repo defence-in-depth layers (shared env scrub, release-gate fail-fast, host-wide audit cap) stop that value from reaching test subprocesses, but they remain the only protection: anything spawned before the scrub that calls `git` itself can still be redirected into the live checkout. The exporting process has not been identified and no setter exists inside this repository.

## Users

- **Agent operators / maintainers** running autonomous agents through herdr/Pi: need every freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables.
- **Contributors** sharing the live checkout: need `dev`/`origin/dev` protected even when a launcher is misconfigured.

User stories:

- As an operator, I want a freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables, so a misconfigured launcher can never redirect a git command into the live checkout.
- As a maintainer, I want the process that sets the override identified and fixed at source, so the defence-in-depth scrub is not the only line of protection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exporting process/script is identified with reproducible, non-destructive evidence (environment of a freshly spawned agent session or a traced process ancestry), and the evidence is recorded in the work item.
- [ ] The export is removed or scoped at source so child processes — panes, `audit_runner`, `run_tests`, and direct `git` calls — never inherit a live-repo `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`.
- [ ] A regression check asserts a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables before any git-touching step; it fails if such a variable is reintroduced.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 (residual launcher risk) is updated to name the confirmed source and the fix, or to record why the source could not be confirmed.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Non-destructive investigation.** The live checkout must never be mutated; evidence gathering must use throwaway/fixture repositories and must never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Source, not symptom.** The fix must be at the exporting launcher, not merely another in-repo scrub layer.
- **Cross-repo (Q1 = A).** The likely launcher lives in the ContextHub repository (`packages/herdr`), outside this worklog's repo. This item owns the investigation and evidence; if ContextHub is confirmed as the culprit, the code fix lands in a **linked cross-repo ContextHub work item**, not in SorraAgents.

## Existing state

Defence-in-depth landed under SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX:

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` + `scrub_repository_overrides` / `repository_override_vars_present` / `log_repository_override_scrub`.
- `skill/test_cache.py::_default_runner`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_run_cmd`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi` pass scrubbed `env=`.
- `run_tests.py --strict-git-env` release-gate fail-fast (invoked by `.githooks/pre-push` for `dev`/`main`).
- `audit_runner.main` host-wide audit cap + `_find_orphaned_audit_processes` / `_warn_on_orphaned_audits`.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 documents the residual external-launcher risk.

Confirmed by search (`rg 'export GIT_|GIT_DIR='` across the repo and tooling): **no setter exists in the SorraAgents repository**. Candidate launchers identified:

- **herdr agent launcher** (ContextHub, external): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` → `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, invoked as `herdr pane run <pane> exec bash run-pi-agent.sh <lease> ...`.
- **herdr downtime worker** (external): `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` forwards `...process.env` to `send-to-pi.sh`, adding only `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` and `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`. It does **not** scrub repository-override vars, so a `GIT_DIR` already present in the herdr process propagates to every spawned pane.
- **git-hook chain** (in repo): `.git/hooks/post-checkout|post-merge|post-rewrite` delegate to `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` → `wl sync`. Git sets `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH` and `GIT_PREFIX` when running hooks, and `implement.py`'s `git_worktree_add` (`git worktree add`) triggers `post-checkout`. The observed `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` + empty `GIT_PREFIX` are the exact git-hook signature, so the poisoned environment was most plausibly inherited from a git-spawned child rather than a static shell `export`.

## Desired change

1. Determine the **origin** of `GIT_DIR` in the launcher environment — which process first set it and why — using non-destructive evidence (Q2 = C): `/proc/<pid>/environ` of pane/agent/audit processes, git `trace2` (`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`) around `git worktree add`/hooks, launcher/hook inspection, followed by **one controlled fresh-session env dump** to prove the end-to-end state.
2. Fix at source: scrub (or refuse to propagate) `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` in the launcher spawn path (e.g. herdr `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`, `run-pi-agent.sh`/`send-to-pi.sh`) and/or stop the git-hook child that leaks the variables. If the culprit is confirmed to be ContextHub/herdr, file the fix as a **linked cross-repo ContextHub work item** (Q1 = A) and note this item's remediation scope.
3. Add a regression check that a fresh agent/test session has no repository-override variables. Ownership follows Q3 = A: the in-repo SorraAgents boundary (launch wrapper / `run_tests.py`) is tested in this repo; the external launcher boundary is tested in a ContextHub test.
4. Update §9.3 with the finding and fix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — update §9.3 with the confirmed source and fix.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — shared override-var list/scrub helper (reuse for any in-repo mitigation or regression check).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — fresh-session regression check and `--strict-git-env` integration.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — orphan/env-evidence hooks for reproducing the audit fan-out condition safely.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add` flow that triggers the `post-checkout` hook.
- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite`, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — hook chain (`wl sync`) executed by git with `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` set.
- External (ContextHub, cross-repo — Q1 = A, fix routed to a linked ContextHub item): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX** – Test/audit runner leaks GIT_DIR into test subprocesses, corrupting the live checkout and origin/dev (parent incident; completed/in_review).
- Children of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX: SA-0MUIULHQC005MUM0 (shared scrub helper), SA-0MUIUMK9Y008SCE0 (scrub in execution paths), SA-0MUIULX49001BWGG (release-gate fail-fast), SA-0MUIULC2Y009XYM1 (regression tests), SA-0MUIUMBL8002HBYH (docs + full suite), SA-0MUIUMO7T00639FL (host-wide audit cap + orphan detection).
- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX** – Restore wl sync: main-checkout git identity was left as incident-era `T <t@t.com>` (residual incident recovery).
- **SA-0MUIBWORE001HOLK** – Symlink nested node_modules into implement worktrees (the worktree whose git dir appeared in the leaked `GIT_DIR`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS0DK6BD001RNDG** – implement.py abort script deletes entire project directory when aborting from main working tree (completed)
- **SA-0MUIBWORE001HOLK** – Symlink nested node_modules into implement worktrees (authoritative record for OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT) (completed)
- **SA-0MPAZORLO00507ZU** – The agents often run tests after commit (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0muia3oe40001qjx, 0muiumo7t00639fl, acceptable, acceptance, actual (+291 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptable, acceptance, actual, add, additional (+260 more)
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — matched: 0muia3oe40001qjx, 0muj2vmf7000uhcx, add, adding, agent (+241 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the incident evidence (process env at the time) is gone; reproduction could itself endanger the live checkout. **Mitigation:** use a throwaway repo + `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`; never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Risk:** fixing only the identified launcher leaves other propagation paths. **Mitigation:** scrub at the launcher spawn boundary (one choke point) plus the regression check.
- **Risk (scope creep):** hardening every launcher is broader than this investigation. **Mitigation:** record additional opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this item.
- **Assumption:** the leak is architectural (environment propagation through the launcher) rather than a one-off manual `export`.
- **Assumption:** the `GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` signature indicates a git-spawned child origin; if tracing shows otherwise, the evidence will redirect the fix.


## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-09**: Plan decomposition — created 5 children in test-first dependency order.
  Evidence tracing (SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K) → controlled dump + regression test
  (SA-0MV0G9BVW008M8AT, SA-0MV0G9CD1007A0IC) → cross-repo fix
  (SA-0MV0G9CT6000LNMA) → docs update (SA-0MV0G9D960078SKT).
  Cross-repo ContextHub fix routed to linked item (per Q1 = A).
## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope / repo):** The candidate launchers are external to SorraAgents (ContextHub `packages/herdr`) and the git-hook chain that runs `wl sync`. Where should the fix land? Options: (A) investigate + evidence in SorraAgents (this item); if herdr is the culprit, file a cross-repo ContextHub work item and link it; (B) fix entirely within SorraAgents by hardening the git hooks / adding a wrapper; (C) transfer this item to ContextHub. **Recommended:** A — keeps the incident record in SorraAgents while routing the actual code change to the repo that owns the launcher. — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-08): A.** Investigation and evidence stay in this SorraAgents item; a confirmed ContextHub/herdr culprit is fixed via a linked cross-repo work item. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (reproduction):** How much live reproduction is acceptable? Options: (A) non-destructive evidence only (`/proc/<pid>/environ`, launcher/hook inspection, git trace2); (B) also spawn a live agent session and dump its env; (C) both. **Recommended:** C — trace2 + launcher inspection first, then one controlled fresh-session env dump to prove the end-to-end state. — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-08): C.** Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (regression-check placement):** The AC "a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables" — where should the check live? Options: (A) an in-repo SorraAgents test of the launch wrapper/`run_tests.py`, with the external launcher covered by its own ContextHub test; (B) in-repo only; (C) ContextHub only. **Recommended:** A — each repo tests the boundary it owns. — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-08): A.** Source: interactive reply.

# PriorityQueue directory lock ignores timeouts — audit slot acquisition can block indefinitely

## Goal (user story)

As an agent running an audit, I want every queue operation in the slot-admission
path to honour its configured timeout, so a peer that holds the queue directory
lock cannot make slot acquisition hang forever.

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/queue.py:282` (`PriorityQueue._acquire_lock`) takes a **blocking**
`fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)` with **no timeout**:

```python
def _acquire_lock(self) -> None:
    lock_path = self._queue_dir / ".lock"
    lock_path.touch(exist_ok=True)
    fd = os.open(str(lock_path), os.O_RDWR)
    fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)      # blocks indefinitely
    self._lock_fd = fd
```

Every public queue operation (`enqueue`, `dequeue`, `peek`, `remove`, `rank`,
`__len__`, `_list_entries`) acquires this lock via `with self._locked()`.
`_acquire_audit_slot()` (audit_runner.py) calls `queue.enqueue`, `queue.rank`,
`queue.peek` and `queue.remove`, so a peer holding `.lock` blocks audit slot
acquisition **without any bound**, defeating the `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`
(default 90 s) and `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 0 s, fail-fast) guarantees.

## Evidence

Minimal reproduction — a child process holds the queue lock for 6 s; the parent
calls `peek(timeout=0)`, whose contract is fail-fast:

```
$ python3 /tmp/queue_hang_demo.py
peek(timeout=0) blocked for 5.50s (contract: ~0s)
```

The timeout argument is not consulted because `_acquire_lock()` blocks **before**
any deadline check. Confirmed against `skill/shared/queue.py` at `dev`
(commit 88a404ec).

## Impact

- A process parked inside the critical section (SIGSTOP, deep I/O stall on the
  lock directory, or a long `_prune_stale` sweep) makes every concurrent audit's
  slot acquisition hang indefinitely — the exact "audit slot acquisition hangs
  indefinitely" symptom reported by an agent (mis-attributed to an unreachable
  `localhost:8000` proxy).
- The priority-queue admission contract (bounded wait, then raise
  `TimeoutError` → "concurrency limit reached" verdict) is not honoured against
  lock contention.
- Contrast: the same package's `Semaphore` uses `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` with a
  bounded retry loop, so this is an inconsistency within the shared layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `PriorityQueue` lock acquisition is **bounded**: a peer holding the directory
   lock cannot block `_acquire_lock`/any public op beyond the configured
   timeout.
2. The configured timeout is honoured on the lock-acquisition path:
   `enqueue` raises `TimeoutError` on deadline, and `dequeue`/`peek` return
   `None` on empty/deadline **without** blocking past it.
3. Implementation follows the existing `Semaphore` pattern (non-blocking
   `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` + short retry loop with a monotonic deadline) or an
   equivalent bounded mechanism; no busy-spin without sleep.
4. Re-entrant behaviour within a single `PriorityQueue` instance is preserved
   (nested `_locked()` remains a no-op when already held).
5. A regression test holds the lock from a second process and asserts that a
   `peek(timeout=0)`/`enqueue(timeout=small)` returns/raises within a bounded
   margin rather than blocking for the hold duration.
6. Existing queue tests (skill/shared/tests/) and the full suite pass.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/queue.py` — `_acquire_lock`, `_release_lock`, `_locked`,
  `enqueue`, `dequeue`, `peek`, `remove`, `rank`.
- `skill/shared/tests/` — queue tests.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_acquire_audit_slot` (consumer).

## Constraints

- Cross-process mutual exclusion must be preserved (no lost updates).
- No new required configuration; existing env vars (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`,
  `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH`, `QUEUE_TTL_SECONDS`) keep working.
- flock releases on process exit / crash must remain the stale-lock guarantee.

## Related Work

- discovered-from:SA-0MUV2UBMT008OE2E (audit slot-status endpoint hardcodes
  localhost). The localhost default was a real bug but **not** the cause of the
  reported hang; this item is the actual unbounded-blocking path.
- SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM — priority-queue admission (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`).
- SA-0MSCC02ME009EGCB — prior audit concurrency investigation.
data.title: PriorityQueue directory lock ignores timeouts — audit slot acquisition can block indefinitely

# Ship release must verify in-scope work items are actually closed before reporting success

## Problem

`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` closes each
candidate with `wl close <id> --force --reason "Shipped in v<version>"` and treats a zero
exit code as success. It never re-reads the item to confirm the persisted
`status`/`stage`. The release then prints `All N work item(s) closed successfully.` — even
when some closes did not persist.

This was demonstrated by the ToneForge v0.1.2 release (2026-10-06): the close step
reported **53/53** closed, but only **50** items ended up `completed`/`done`. Three
remained `completed`/`in_review` with no close comment and unchanged `updatedAt`:

| Item | Title |
|---|---|
| TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18 | Add CLI command to register new primitive recipes |
| TF-0MUUELBUD002OEQ8 | Repair main checkout node_modules symlink loop blocking npm/vitest |
| TF-0MMZIW9NQ09MV98G | Convert hard-coded recipes to ToneGraph configs |

Root cause is the `wl` lost-update race fixed/tracked in ContextHub: a concurrent
`wl sync` clobbered the three in-flight closes (see **WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ** under
WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7). The ship skill cannot prevent that race, but it **can** detect it:
right now a lost close is silently reported as a successful release.

## Desired behaviour

After the close step, re-read every attempted candidate and confirm it is terminal
(`status == "completed"` and `stage == "done"`). If any are not:

1. Re-attempt the close once (bounded), then re-verify.
2. Report unclosed items explicitly by id in the release summary — never include them in
   the "closed" count or claim "all closed successfully".
3. Make the discrepancy visible in the step result (e.g. `unclosedCount` /
   `unclosedItems`) so the operator sees the true outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` verifies persisted state (injectable read boundary) for
   each attempted close instead of trusting only the close command's exit code.
2. An item that exits 0 but is not `completed`/`done` is counted as unclosed and listed by
   id; the summary/return value reflects it and does not claim blanket success.
3. A transient lost close is retried at least once before being reported unclosed.
4. Regression tests with injected `getCandidateItemsFn` / `runCloseCommand` /
   verification boundary cover: (a) all closes persist → success; (b) one close is a no-op
   (exit 0, state unchanged) → retried, then reported unclosed; (c) retry re-persists →
   reported closed.
5. `npm run build` and existing ship suites pass.

## Notes

- Root-cause fix is on the `wl` side: WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ (lock `wl close`; child of the
  WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7 lost-update umbrella).
- Related: SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP (close step *falsely refuses* parents with done
  descendants — fixed by SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9 / SA-0MUTYRYEM000EEF7).
- Refiled to ContextHub: SA-0MUX8PYAY0008HFZ (the raw race report) → WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ.
data.title: Ship release must verify in-scope work items are actually closed before reporting success

Discovered while implementing SA-0MUMHR0BT007IKAL (discovered-from:SA-0MUMHR0BT007IKAL).

## Problem
Two or more full test-suite runs executing concurrently on the same host deadlock. Observed twice today: two pytest full-suite processes (one per agent worktree) both stalled in hrtimer_nanosleep with <30s CPU after ~30-40 min, and both recovered only when one run was killed (the surviving run resumed immediately).

## Root cause (hypothesis)
TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY defaults to 2. Each outer run_tests.py holds one `test` semaphore slot for the duration of the suite. The suite itself contains tests that invoke nested `run_tests.py` (tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestRunTestsGuardFires) which need another `test` slot. With two outer runs holding both slots, the nested acquires wait indefinitely (TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT inherited from the parent, e.g. 10800s), producing a deadlock. Setting TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 for one run let its nested acquires use the spare slots and avoided the deadlock.

## Secondary flake
tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs calls syncDevWithMain() which runs live `git fetch`/`git push` against the real repo; under concurrent load it hung in ep_poll (socket) and blocked the pre-push full-suite gate. This test is non-hermetic and should be made hermetic (inject/fake the git operations).

## Desired outcome
- Full-suite runs on a shared host must not deadlock (reserve headroom for nested run_tests slots, or make the nested-aware tests use an isolated semaphore dir / PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR).
- tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs must not perform live git fetch/push.

## Evidence
- /tmp/finish-SA-0MUMHR0BT007IKAL.log (slot wait + full-suite gate).
- Kill of one stalled pytest unstuck the other (wchan hrtimer_nanosleep -> poll_schedule_timeout -> R).
data.title: Test infra: concurrent full-suite runs deadlock on the host-wide test semaphore

## Problem

The local skill extensions convention (`.pi/skills_extensions/<skill>/`, contract SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0) is consumed only by the test skill. The implement skill never calls `load_extension()`, so a project-local extension for implement is inert: its `SKILL_PREFIX.md` is never surfaced and its `extension.json` is ignored.

This blocks consuming projects that need project-specific implement behaviour — concretely, `open_source_llm` (OSL-0MUYC0UEN003C1M6) wants uncommitted `.llm-wiki/` content to be exempt from the dirty-tree gate.

## Expected

- `implement.py` loads `.pi/skills_extensions/implement/` via the shared `load_extension()` helper; absence is a no-op (byte-for-byte unchanged behaviour).
- Project-local prose hooks (`SKILL_PREFIX.md` / `SKILL_POSTFIX.md`) are surfaced to the agent at the documented points.
- A project can declare that specific dirty paths are expected and must not hard-fail `implement.py start`/`finish`; the exemption is project-scoped, explicit, and additive (never weakens the build → test → commit order).
- The worktree placement gate (`_worktree_placement_violation()`) uses the same exemption logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Absent extension: implement behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] Present extension: prose hooks are surfaced before the first actionable step and after the final step.
- [ ] Present extension declaring an expected-dirty path (e.g. `.llm-wiki/`): `implement.py start` does not abort on that path; non-declared dirty paths still abort.

# implement.py start fails to claim an open work item (invalid stage)

## Problem
With the installed Worklog CLI (wl 0.1.19), `wl update --stage in_progress` is rejected: valid stages are `idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done`. `phase_start` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` claims via `StatusLifecycle.update_status(id, 'in_progress', stage='in_progress', ...)`, so claiming an `open` item fails outright:

```
wl ... update SA-... --status in_progress --json --stage in_progress --assignee Map
RuntimeError: Invalid stage "in_progress". Valid stages: idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done.
```

When the item is already `in-progress`, only the stage update fails and `phase_start` logs a WARNING and proceeds. When the item is `open`, the combined update fails and `implement.py start` returns `success: false` — the normal (open -> in_progress) claim path is broken.

## Impact
Every `implement.py start` / `finish` on a freshly-opened item cannot claim it; agents must claim manually with a status-only update. Blocks the deterministic implement workflow.

## Expected
Claiming sets `status=in_progress` without an invalid stage (preserve the current stage or use a valid one). The StatusLifecycle claim path should not pass `stage='in_progress'` on a wl build that does not accept it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `implement.py start <id>` on an `open` item succeeds and sets `status=in_progress`.
- [ ] No `--stage in_progress` is sent to `wl` (or it is only sent when the installed wl supports it).
- [ ] Regression test asserts the claim path does not fail on a wl build whose stage enum excludes `in_progress`.
data.title: implement.py start cannot claim an open item: sets invalid stage in_progress (wl 0.1.19)

# Add guarded_run_all to run_tests.py

## Goal

Expose a **programmatic guard-owning entry point** in `run_tests.py` so that
`implement.py` can delegate test execution through the canonical runner without
shelling out to a subprocess.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `run_tests.py` exports a `guarded_run_all` function (callable from
  outside the module) that:
  1. Checks `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE_ENV` — if set, stands down (outer guard
     already owns); else sets `guard_active = True`.
  2. When `guard_active`: snapshots the checkout via
     `snapshot_repo_state(project_root)`.
  3. Sets `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE_ENV = "1"` before calling `run_all`.
  4. Calls `run_all(...)` with the same signature as the existing `run_all`.
  5. Always clears the marker (`os.environ.pop(...)`) in a `finally` block.
  6. When `guard_active`: checks for mutation via
     `_detect_live_repo_mutation(project_root, snapshot_before)` and merges
     any mutation into the result (sets `success = False`, adds
     `live_repo_mutation` key).
  7. Returns the `run_all` result dict.

- **AC2** `main()` delegates to `guarded_run_all` (no code duplication — the
  guard logic moves entirely into `guarded_run_all`).

- **AC3** The function signature accepts `cwd: Path | None`, `timeout: int`,
  `scope: str`, `base_ref: str`, and all other kwargs that `run_all` accepts.
  The result is the same dict shape as `run_all`.

- **AC4** No behavioural change to the CLI: `run_tests.py --json` and
  non-JSON output must work exactly as before.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Add `guarded_run_all`, refactor `main()`
  to call it.

## Constraints

- Do **not** duplicate the snapshot/mutation logic — it must live in exactly one
  place.
- `guarded_run_all` is the *single* source of truth for guard ownership.
- Preserve the existing `run_all` function signature and return type.
- Graceful degradation: if the test skill is unavailable, `implement.py`
  continues to use the current inner-guard path (handled in the next sub-task).
data.title: Add guarded_run_all to run_tests.py — guard-owning programmatic API

# Update implement.py run_tests to delegate to guarded_run_all

## Goal

Route `implement.py`'s test execution through `run_tests.py`'s
`guarded_run_all` so the canonical outer snapshot guard always owns the
checkout, even when `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` is pre-set in the environment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `implement.py` imports `guarded_run_all` from
  `test.scripts.run_tests` (same import pattern already used for
  `full_suite_commands`, `changed_scope_commands`, etc.). When the import
  fails, it falls back to the current inner-guard path.

- **AC2** When the test skill is available, `run_tests()` in `implement.py`:
  1. Resolves full-suite commands via `full_suite_commands(cwd)` (already done).
  2. Calls `guarded_run_all(cwd=Path(cwd), timeout=..., scope=...,
     base_ref=...)` — with the commands passed via the `commands` kwarg.
  3. Adapts `guarded_run_all`'s result dict (which has `suites`, `failures`,
     `success`, `scope`, `timing`) into `implement.py`'s expected result
     format (`exit_code`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `failures`, `success`,
     `skipped`, `tooling`, `scope`).
  4. Preserves `run_cached` cache sharing: `guarded_run_all` calls
     `run_suite` → `run_cached` with the same keys/scope metadata.
  5. Preserves semaphore pacing: `guarded_run_all` uses the same concurrency
     control as the CLI path.

- **AC3** When `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` is already set (nested run),
  `guarded_run_all` stands down (outer guard already owns), and `implement.py`
  does NOT arm a second guard — the result is still guarded because the outer
  runner owns it.

- **AC4** When `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` is NOT set (direct implement.py run),
  `guarded_run_all` arms the outer guard (snapshot → run → check mutation).

- **AC5** Existing `implement.py` test behaviour is unchanged: changed-scope
  selection, named groups, `run_cached` caching keys, host-wide test-semaphore
  pacing, the `skipped`/`tooling` result contract.

- **AC6** Graceful degradation: when the test skill is unavailable,
  `implement.py` continues its current path (direct `run_cached` calls with
  the inner guard only).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Update `run_tests`,
  `_run_resolved_suite`, `_run_commands`, `_run_changed_scope_pytest` to
  delegate to `guarded_run_all` when available.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `guarded_run_all` (from sub-task 1).

## Implementation Notes

The result adaptation from `guarded_run_all`→`implement.py` format:

```python
def _adapt_guarded_result(guarded_result, tooling, scope):
    """Convert guarded_run_all result to implement.py result format."""
    return {
        "success": guarded_result["success"],
        "stdout": "",  # guarded_run_all aggregates per-suite; aggregate here
        "stderr": "",
        "exit_code": 0 if guarded_result["success"] else 1,
        "failures": guarded_result.get("failures", []),
        "skipped": False,
        "tooling": tooling,
        "scope": guarded_result.get("scope", scope),
        "live_repo_mutation": guarded_result.get("live_repo_mutation"),
    }
```

## Constraints

- Do **not** change the CLI interface of `run_tests.py`.
- Preserve `run_cached` cache key identity: same command + scope = same cache
  entry as if the CLI path ran it.
- Preserve semaphore pacing: `guarded_run_all` uses the same concurrency
  control (`_test_concurrency_slot`) as the CLI path.
- No test-weakening: no skips/xfails/retries to reach green.
data.title: Update implement.py run_tests to delegate to guarded_run_all with graceful fallback

# Add guard-ownership regression tests and update documentation

## Goal

Add regression tests that prove guard ownership parity at the boundary between
`implement.py` and the canonical runner, and update all related documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (regression test — guard ownership)** In
  `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` (or a new `skill/implement/tests/`
  file), add a test that:
  1. Sets `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE=1` in the environment.
  2. Calls `run_tests.py`'s `guarded_run_all` programmatically (or invokes
     `implement.py run_tests` which delegates to it).
  3. Mutates the checkout during the run.
  4. Asserts the mutation is detected (non-zero result, `live_repo_mutation`
     key present).
  This proves that even when the marker is pre-set, a nested `guarded_run_all`
  call still works correctly (stands down, outer guard owns).

- **AC2 (regression test — clean run)** Add a test that:
  1. Calls `guarded_run_all` (or `implement.py run_tests`) with a clean
     checkout.
  2. Asserts no guard failure (exit 0, no `live_repo_mutation` key).

- **AC3 (regression test — no double-guard)** Add a test that:
  1. Calls `guarded_run_all` from a context where `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` is
     NOT set.
  2. Asserts the marker IS set during the run (inner guard stands down).
  3. Asserts the outer guard owns the checkout (snapshot taken, mutation
     detected).
  4. Asserts the marker is cleared after the run.

- **AC4 (implement.py existing tests preserved)** All existing
  `tests/test_implement_run_tests_*.py` suites stay green.

- **AC5 (documentation)** Update documentation:
  - `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — add a comment documenting the
    guard-ownership contract: `guarded_run_all` in `run_tests.py` is the single
    source of truth for outer guard ownership; `implement.py` delegates to it.
  - `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — document `guarded_run_all` in its
    module docstring.
  - `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — update `run_tests` docstring to
    describe the delegation to `guarded_run_all`.
  - `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — if it documents the test step, update to
    mention the guard-ownership contract.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` — Add guard-ownership regression
  tests.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — Update documentation.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Update documentation.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Update documentation.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Update if needed.

## Constraints

- No skips/xfails/retries to reach green.
- Tests must use `tmp_path` repositories (no live checkout mutation).
- Follow the existing test patterns in
  `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`.

## Summary

Non-destructive investigation into the environment propagation chain that exports `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, and `GIT_CONFIG*` into agent/test sessions. This uses `/proc/<pid>/environ` inspection, git `trace2` (`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`), and launcher/hook inspection to produce reproducible evidence without mutating the live checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/proc/<pid>/environ` of an active agent/pane process is captured (or a representative trace is produced) showing the inherited environment.
- [ ] Git `trace2` (`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`) around `git worktree add` and hook execution demonstrates where repository-overriding variables are set.
- [ ] The full propagation chain is documented: which process first sets the variable, through which intermediaries, and into which final target.
- [ ] Evidence is recorded as a comment on this work item with non-destructive proof.
- [ ] A controlled fresh-session env dump proves the end-to-end state (one controlled run).

## Implementation

1. **Inspect git hooks and trace2:** Use `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` to capture the environment at hook execution time. Create a throwaway repo to test `git worktree add` and verify whether git itself sets repository-overriding vars in the hook subprocess environment.
2. **Inspect ContextHub spawn options:** Review `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` in `downtime-worker.ts` — it spreads `...process.env`, confirming a propagation path if the herdr process itself has a repository override set.
3. **Inspect send-to-pi.sh and run-pi-agent.sh:** Confirm they do not set or filter git variables.
4. **One controlled env dump:** Spawn a single agent session and capture its environment before any `git` touch.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` list for reference.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — scrub infrastructure.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 — current residual risk documentation.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (ContextHub).
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh` — launcher scripts (ContextHub).
- `.githooks/post-checkout|post-merge|post-rewrite`, `worklog-post-pull` — hook chain.
data.title: GIT_DIR evidence: trace non-destructive env propagation path

An in-repo SorraAgents regression test that asserts a freshly launched agent/test session inherits no repository-override git variables before any git-touching step. This tests the SorraAgents boundary (the launch wrapper / `run_tests.py`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test exists that verifies `run_tests.py` scrubs repository-override variables from spawned subprocess environments.
- [ ] The test covers the case where the parent process inherits a `GIT_DIR` — the scrub must remove it.
- [ ] The test asserts `repository_override_vars_present()` returns empty for the scrubbed environment.
